proposals.name: Unseen microlens magnification
proposals.idea: An unseen point lens passed in front of a red background source, producing the accelerating r-band rise before the observational gap and a sharp peak hidden within it. The TDE fit extrapolated that rise into a luminous plateau, but the source is now demagnifying symmetrically back toward its steady baseline.
proposals.predicts: Future g and r fluxes will follow the same achromatic lens profile, mirroring the rise, and asymptote to a constant red baseline with g-r about 1.1 rather than remaining bright and blue.

proposals.name: Galactic microlensing event
proposals.idea: An unseen compact foreground lens crossed the line of sight to a background star, so the early brightening was increasing magnification rather than an explosion or accretion flare. The event peaked between the early r-band rise and the later faint points and is now demagnifying.
proposals.predicts: It predicts one achromatic, approximately time-symmetric peak at the same time in g and r, followed by a return to the constant pre-event source-plus-blend baseline, rather than continued TDE brightening or colour-evolving supernova decay.

proposals.name: Stray-light template residual flare
proposals.idea: A bright off-axis star leaked stray light into the r-band template subtraction, producing a smooth spurious rise in the first epoch that peaked during the observing gap and vanished after the template or pointing changed. The later g and r detections are only the steady underlying source, misread by the SN and TDE fits as the tail of a huge explosion.
proposals.predicts: Future flux remains at the steady per-band baseline, with any residuals repeating with pointing, seeing, or template epoch rather than fading smoothly to zero.

proposals.name: Passed microlensing peak
proposals.idea: An unseen point lens crossed a steady background source, and the early brightening was rising magnification rather than an explosion or accretion flare. The alignment peaked unobserved between days -24 and -8, so the source is now demagnifying toward its unlensed level.
proposals.predicts: It predicts an achromatic, time-symmetric decline with a fixed g/r flux ratio toward a constant baseline, not the much brighter continued peak forecast by the TDE and SN Ia hypotheses.

proposals.name: Microlensed red background star
proposals.idea: The early r-band brightening was the approach to peak magnification, not an explosion or accretion rise, and the transient peaked in the unobserved gap before fading by day -8. A point lens magnifying a steady red background star produces the same magnification in g and r, so both bands rise and fall together while preserving the source colour.
proposals.predicts: It predicts a symmetric achromatic decline mirroring the earlier rise and a return to the same constant red baseline, rather than a blue slowly declining TDE plateau or colour-evolving supernova.
